transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously what’s happening with my dad’s lab results. For about a year now, I’ve been seeing things in his chart that don’t match what I saw before, like parts are changed or held back. The doctors keep saying the numbers are fine, and my family thinks I’m overreacting, but I know what I saw. It’s been wearing me down.
Have you ever felt that information or records were being altered or withheld in a way that others don’t seem to notice, even when they check?

Yes. That’s basically what I’ve been trying to explain. For about a year, I’ve felt like parts of my dad’s lab results are being changed or not shown in the chart. Other people look and say everything is fine, but it doesn’t match what I remember seeing. I know what I saw, and it’s been really wearing me down.
Have you ever had experiences outside of your dad’s lab results where you felt information was being hidden or altered in a way others don’t seem to notice?
No, not really. I mean, I haven’t noticed it with other things the way I have with my dad’s lab results. That’s the main thing that keeps standing out to me.
Have you ever had a strong belief about something that others have told you is not true, but you still felt certain about it, even when they provided evidence against it?

Yes. That’s what this whole thing has been. I’ve been trying for the past year to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. Doctors keep telling me the numbers are fine, my family says I’m seeing something that isn’t there, but I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I’m certain of it, and it’s been wearing me down.
Even when doctors have shown you the current lab results and explained that they don’t match what you remember, do you still feel certain that the records have been changed or withheld?

Yes. Even when they show me the current results and explain it, I still feel like something’s off. I know what I saw before, and the chart now doesn’t match that. It feels like parts of the results were changed or held back, and no one else is taking it seriously. It’s been exhausting trying to prove it.
Have you ever had strong, fixed beliefs that others said were not true, even when you were shown proof, but those beliefs were not related to your dad’s lab results?

No, not outside of that. The thing I’m stuck on is my dad’s lab results. For the past year I’ve been trying to prove someone in the clinic system changed or held back part of them. Even when doctors and my family say everything is fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. That’s the belief that’s been wearing me down.
Have you ever had any beliefs that others said were not true, and you were completely sure about even when they showed you proof, that weren’t related to your dad’s lab results?

No, not really. It’s just been this one thing with my dad’s lab results. I know people keep telling me the numbers are fine and showing me what’s in the chart, but it doesn’t match what I remember seeing. I’m not completely sure like that about other things—this is the thing I can’t let go of.
Have you ever had any other experiences where you felt certain about something that others didn’t agree with, even if they showed you evidence, outside of your concern with your dad’s lab results?

No, not really outside of that. It’s this situation with my dad’s lab results that I can’t get past. I’ve been trying for about a year to prove someone in the clinic system changed something or held part of it back. People keep telling me the numbers are fine, but I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw, and it’s just wearing me down.
Have you ever had any experiences where you were completely sure something was true, but others said it wasn’t, even when they showed you proof, that wasn’t related to your dad’s lab results?

No, not really. It’s just this thing with my dad’s lab results. I’ve been trying for the past year to prove someone in the clinic system changed them or held part of them back. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine and showing me the chart, but I know it doesn’t match what I saw. It’s been wearing me down.
Even though others have shown you the current lab results and explained that they are unchanged, do you still feel certain that someone altered the records, without any doubt?

Yes. I know how it sounds, but yes, I’m still certain. They keep showing me the current chart and saying nothing changed, and my family says the numbers are fine, but it doesn’t match what I saw before. I feel like someone in the clinic system changed it or held something back, and I can’t just let that go. It’s been wearing me down.
Even though doctors have shown you the current lab results and explained that they haven't changed, do you still believe with absolute certainty that someone altered the records, without any doubt?

Yes. I know they keep saying it hasn’t changed, and they show me what’s in the chart now, but I’m still sure something was changed or held back. It doesn’t match what I saw before. I’ve been trying to prove it for about a year, and it’s just… it’s really wearing me down.
Has there been a time when you realized, even for a moment, that your belief about your dad’s lab results being altered might not be true, even after others showed you the records?

No. I mean, I’ve tried to consider what they’re saying, but it doesn’t last, because I know what I saw before doesn’t match what’s in the chart now. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine, but I still feel sure someone changed something or held part of it back. That’s why I’ve been stuck on it for this long.
Has there been any point where you questioned, even slightly, that your belief about your dad’s lab results being altered might not be accurate, even after seeing the records again?

No, not really. I’ve tried to listen when they show me the records again and say the numbers are fine, but I still know the chart doesn’t match what I saw before. I’ve spent the past year trying to prove someone in the clinic system changed something or held part of it back, and it’s wearing me down.

Have you ever experienced any strange sensations, heard voices, or had thoughts that felt foreign to you, or believed things that others might find unusual, outside of your concern with your dad’s lab results?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or felt like thoughts were put in my head or anything like that. It’s really just this issue with my dad’s lab results.
